rejected.title: Allegory
card: An allegory is a story with two levels of meaning. On the surface it tells a story. Underneath, its characters and events stand for ideas or real events.
Animal Farm by George Orwell is a well-known allegory. On the surface, farm animals take over their farm. Underneath, the animals and events stand for real people and events in history.
To read an allegory, ask what each main character and event could stand for. Then check that the meanings fit together across the whole story.
A writer may use an allegory to comment on ideas such as greed, power or courage, or on real events, in a way that is indirect and easy to remember.
rejected.remember: An allegory is a story that works on two levels: what happens, and what it stands for.

a.q: What makes a story an allegory?
opts: A story whose characters and events stand for ideas
A story that compares two things using like or as
A story told by one of the characters in it
A story that names a thing by something linked to it
a.why: An allegory has a surface story and a deeper meaning, with characters and events standing for ideas or real events. The comparison with like or as describes a simile, which is a single comparison, not a whole story.
a.clue: Think about a story that means something more underneath.

b.q: Ana writes a story about a small bird shut out of a walled garden by bigger birds. She says it is really about a newcomer trying to fit into a town. Why does this make it an allegory?
opts: Its events carry a second meaning about real people
Its main character is a bird rather than a person
Its plot has a clear beginning, middle and end
Its walled garden is described in careful detail
b.why: The bird's struggle is the surface story, and a newcomer's experience is the meaning underneath, so the story works on two levels. Having an animal character is not enough, because many stories about animals have no deeper meaning.
b.clue: Ask whether the story works on more than one level.

version.title: Allegory
card: An allegory is a story with two levels. On the surface, things happen to characters. Underneath, the characters and events stand for ideas or real events.
George Orwell's novel Animal Farm (1945) is a well-known allegory. Farm animals drive out their farmer, but the story stands for the Russian Revolution and the rule that followed it.
In an allegory, the whole story carries the second meaning, not just one object or one line. Its main characters and events each have a match underneath.

Writers can use allegory to explore ideas such as power, greed or fairness, or to comment on real events indirectly. Readers work out what each part stands for and check that the meanings fit together.
version.remember: An allegory tells one story on the surface and another underneath.

a.q: Which of these is an allegory?
opts: A tale where two ant nests stand for warring countries
A tale where a red scarf returns at every sad moment
A tale with one line comparing a flooded river to a snake
A tale told by an ant who speaks directly to the reader
a.why: When two ant nests stand for warring countries, the whole story has a second meaning, which makes it an allegory. A scarf that returns is one object with a meaning, not a whole story that stands for something else.
a.clue: Which tale has a second meaning running through the whole story?

b.q: Ravi's story follows a lion who takes all the food in the forest, until the smaller animals join together and stop him. Ravi says it is about people standing up to an unfair ruler. What makes it an allegory?
opts: The whole story stands for an idea about power
The lion is an animal that acts like a person
The forest is described with rich sense detail
The lion appears again at each important moment
b.why: The lion, the smaller animals and what happens to them all match a second meaning about standing up to unfair rulers, so the story works on two levels. Animals that act like people appear in many stories with no hidden meaning, so that alone does not make an allegory.
b.clue: Does the second meaning run through the whole story?

a.best: A tale where two ant nests stand for warring countries

b.best: The whole story stands for an idea about power

problems.detail: The clue asks whether the second meaning runs through "the whole story", and the right option is the only one that says "The whole story", so a student can match the words without knowing the idea. A clue that points to the idea without repeating the right option's words would test more.
